title: Personal data of 110,000 members of healthcare services provider Alliance Medinet compromised
gist: On Oct 24, Alliance Healthcare Group reported that a cyber incident compromised the personal data of about 110,000 members of healthcare services provider Alliance Medinet. Potentially affected details include names, personal identification numbers, and contact information, with some corporate customers of Income Insurance and Singlife also involved. Alliance Healthcare Group said affected members are being notified while investigations continue.

title: Singapore’s core inflation eases to 2% in September on lower services, retail prices
gist: Singapore's core inflation eased to 2 per cent year-on-year in September from 2.2 per cent in August, according to figures released on Friday (Oct 23) by MAS and METI. Overall inflation fell to 2.2 per cent, even as food inflation rose to 2.4 per cent and accommodation inflation edged up to 0.9 per cent. MAS and METI expect inflation to remain slightly elevated in the immediate quarters ahead before easing more discernibly from mid-2027.

Even as respondents anticipate a slight increase in expenses, most expect their household financial conditions to remain unchanged over the next year.

title: What is the cut-off yield of the latest T-bill?
gist: The 6-month T-bill issued on 29 September 2026, BS26119F, was cut off at 1.92 per cent a year. The one issued a fortnight earlier, BS26118E on 15 September 2026, was cut off at 1.70 per cent. Open the MAS page on the day before you quote it, and never set a T-bill yield against an insurance return as though they were the same thing.

title: Woman loses suit against Prudential after S$100,000 brain aneurysm surgery claim denied, says she plans to appeal
gist: Cai Yanhong collapsed on a bus in 2023 with a ruptured brain aneurysm and had an emergency endovascular repair, a minimally invasive procedure, at the National University Hospital. Her PruLife Multiplier policy, bought in 2016, covered brain aneurysm surgery only as a surgical craniotomy, an open-skull procedure. Endovascular repair was not covered, so the S$108,500 claim was denied. She argued that she was unconscious and had no say in which surgery was performed, and that the procedure the policy did cover was the riskier one. In a judgment published 3 September 2026, District Judge Teo Guan Kee dismissed the claim. He found no "secret or hidden redefining" of the term, noting she had initialled the product summary and had 14 days to cancel. Prudential said: "The court has affirmed that the claim was assessed in line with the policy contract," and said it would look into waiving any court-ordered costs as a gesture of goodwill. The claimant said she will most likely appeal.
talkingPoint: The insurer won, and that is exactly why it is worth reading. The client's protection is the wording, not the diagnosis. Careful: The insurer won this case. Saying or implying that Prudential acted wrongly is both wrong and legally risky. Carry the outcome and the insurer's statement whenever you carry this clipping.

title: Shield Plan and IP rider changes: This is your 2026 update
gist: Income repriced Enhanced IncomeShield from 1 April 2026: an average of 14 per cent on Preferred, 13 per cent on Advantage and 7 per cent on Basic. Income, Raffles and Singlife all revised their main Shield plan premiums up in the same round. Income's new Optima Care and Essential Care riders came in 23 to 24 per cent cheaper on Preferred and 47 to 48 per cent cheaper on Advantage than the riders they replaced. Optima Care holds the 5 per cent co-payment on panel doctors but raises it to 8 per cent off panel. Essential Care cuts the panel co-payment from 10 per cent to 7 per cent.
talkingPoint: Two numbers moved in opposite directions on the same page. Add them up for the client rather than letting them read only the one that frightens them. Careful: An adviser platform's summary, not a regulator's, and it covers Income, Raffles and Singlife only. Check any figure against that insurer's own notice before you quote it.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Base plan up, new rider down, in the same letter. Worth adding the two together before deciding how you feel about the total.

Source: iFAST Global Markets, 24 Aug 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: AIA delivers strong first half results in 2026
gist: AIA Singapore's Total Weighted Premium Income rose 17 per cent in the first half of 2026, and Annualised New Premium rose 14 per cent to US$644 million. AIA Group reported operating profit after tax of US$4,163 million, up 13 per cent per share, and value of new business of US$3,212 million. 2026 is AIA Singapore's 95th year here, and its twelfth as Singapore's number one Million Dollar Round Table company.
talkingPoint: A Shield plan is a promise with a sixty-year tail. Put this beside the ownership clippings and ask who they would rather be insured with in 2050. Careful: Financial strength is not claims performance, and a results headline is not a promise about any one claim. Never let it stand in for how a claim gets paid.

title: Removal of the 15-month Wait-out Period for Private Residential Property Owners Purchasing Non-Subsidised HDB Resale Flats
gist: With immediate effect, private property owners and ex-owners buying a non-subsidised HDB resale flat without an HDB loan no longer serve a 15-month wait-out period. The wait-out was introduced on 30 September 2022 as a cooling measure. Citizens aged 55 and above were already exempt if they moved to a 4-room or smaller flat. HDB gave the reason: resale prices fell for two consecutive quarters in 2026, by 0.1 per cent in Q1 and 0.3 per cent in Q2, after five quarters of slower or no growth. A private owner must still dispose of their private property, in Singapore or overseas, within six months of completing the HDB purchase.
talkingPoint: For anyone who has talked about downgrading to release money for retirement, the fifteen-month gap that made it unworkable has gone. That conversation is live again. Careful: It applies only to a non-subsidised resale flat bought without an HDB loan, and the six-month disposal rule still stands. Check the client's own HFE letter status before planning around it.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Selling a private property and buying an HDB resale flat no longer means waiting 15 months. If downgrading was ever part of your retirement plan, the timing just changed.

Source: Housing & Development Board, 28 Jul 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: MAS Monetary Policy Statement - July 2026
gist: MAS increased the rate of appreciation of the policy band very slightly, building on a larger tightening in April 2026. The band's width and centre are unchanged. MAS Core Inflation ran at 1.5 per cent year on year in Q2 2026, up from 1.2 per cent in January and February, driven by fuel, non-cooked food and imported goods. For 2026 as a whole, both MAS Core Inflation and CPI-All Items inflation are projected to average 1.5 to 2.5 per cent, easing more discernibly only in the second half of 2027. The economy grew 5.7 per cent year on year in Q2 2026 on advance estimates, ahead of expectations, so the positive output gap is now forecast to widen.
talkingPoint: Singapore has no policy interest rate, it steers the currency. So when a client asks what the central bank is doing about prices, the honest answer is that it tightened twice this year and still expects inflation to run into 2027. Careful: MAS manages the exchange rate, not an interest rate, so do not describe this as a rate rise. And never present an inflation forecast as a reason to buy a particular product; it is context for a conversation, not a recommendation.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Singapore's central bank tightened policy again in July because inflation is expected to stay elevated into early 2027. Prices rising faster than your savings is the quiet risk in holding a lot of cash.

Source: Monetary Authority of Singapore, 27 Jul 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: The longer we live, the more we worry: AIA Longevity Study finds Singaporeans view longevity with more anxiety than opportunity
gist: More than half of Singaporeans, 51 per cent, see living longer as more of a concern than an opportunity. Only 22 per cent see it as an opportunity. Singaporeans expect to live to 80.2 and expect their health to start declining at 70.2, a ten-year gap between lifespan and healthspan. 53 per cent say they feel uncertain when they think about growing older. Financial preparedness is the weakest of the four pillars, with 61 per cent concerned about running out of retirement savings. Younger Singaporeans are more worried than older ones, and expect an even longer gap.
talkingPoint: The best opening line on this wall. Ask a client how long they expect to live, then how long they expect to stay well. The gap they name is the conversation, and you have not mentioned a product yet. Careful: AIA's own study, so attribute it as AIA research rather than independent data, and quote the figures as what people EXPECT, not as a forecast of how long anyone will live.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Singaporeans expect to live to about 80 but expect their health to start declining around 70. That ten-year gap is the part of retirement most plans forget to fund.

Source: AIA Singapore, 23 Jul 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Allianz to buy HSBC's Singapore insurance unit for $2.09 billion
gist: Allianz announced on 24 July 2026 (Singapore time) that it had agreed to acquire HSBC Life Singapore for about 2.0 billion euros. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to approval from the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The deal comes with a 15-year exclusive bancassurance agreement with HSBC Bank Singapore.
talkingPoint: If your client holds an HSBC Shield plan, the company behind it is changing owner again, and the sale is not even closed yet. Careful: A sale is not a claims problem. Nothing here says HSBC Life pays claims badly. Keep it to who will own the policy.

title: Majulah Package
gist: Every Singaporean born in 1973 or earlier gets at least one part of the Majulah Package. It reaches about 1.6 million people. The yearly Earn and Save Bonus goes to those earning an average of $500 to $6,000 a month, living in a home with an annual value of $31,000 or less, and owning no more than one property. The one-time Retirement Savings Bonus and MediSave Bonus were paid in December 2024. Each year's Earn and Save Bonus is assessed on the previous Year of Assessment's income and on property as at 30 November of the preceding year. Nothing to apply for.
talkingPoint: Ask a client in their fifties or early sixties whether they got theirs. Most cannot say, because it lands in a CPF account rather than a bank account and no letter demands a reply. Careful: The bonus amount is tiered by income and the page is a scheme summary, not a dated announcement. Check the client's own eligibility on the GovBenefits e-service rather than quoting a figure at them.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

If you were born in 1973 or earlier you qualify for at least one part of the Majulah Package, and the Earn and Save Bonus repeats every year you are working and eligible. It is paid automatically into your CPF.

Source: Government of Singapore, Updated 8 Jul 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Measures to manage increases to base Integrated Shield Plan premiums
gist: Over the three years from December 2021 to December 2024, private hospital IP premiums rose every year at an average of 8.6 per cent, and private hospital rider premiums at an average of 17.2 per cent. Two MPs asked whether insurers were raising base premiums at the same moment the new riders cut rider premiums. MOH confirmed some plans were repriced in that round. MOH put the saving from moving to a new rider at 35 to 40 per cent on average. MAS rules require an insurer to tell policyholders at least 30 days before any change to policy terms takes effect.
talkingPoint: Nobody is coming to cap the price. Ask the client what they want to do about the part they can still control, which is the plan and rider they sit on. Careful: These are market-wide averages across all private hospital plans, not any one insurer's increase. Never present them as AIA's, or as a competitor's.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Your Shield plan premium is not rising because of anything you did. Across the market, base premiums have gone up 8.6 per cent a year and riders 17.2 per cent, and the Health Ministry does not set either.

Source: Ministry of Health, 6 May 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Figure of 16.9% an inaccurate depiction of healthcare cost inflation
gist: MOH wrote to the Straits Times forum page about its 30 March 2026 report on medical cost inflation. The Healthcare Consumer Price Index for 2025 is about 3 per cent, covering hospital bills, primary care and medication. MOH named the cause of the claims growth as overly generous coverage, leading to what it called a "buffet syndrome", and said that is why it required the change to rider design.
talkingPoint: Bring this one out before the client hears the 16.9 per cent number somewhere else. Healthcare did not get 17 per cent dearer. Private insurance claims did, and MOH says why. Careful: Carry this card with the WTW one, never instead of it. Quoting 16.9 per cent as Singapore's healthcare inflation is the specific claim MOH corrected in print.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

If you have seen the figure of 16.9 per cent, it is the growth in private insurance claims, not the cost of healthcare. The Health Ministry put healthcare inflation at about 3 per cent for 2025.

Source: Ministry of Health, 13 Apr 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: 10 Weeks of Shared Parental Leave From 1 April 2026
gist: Parents of Singapore Citizen children born on or after 1 April 2026 get 10 weeks of Shared Parental Leave, up from 6, to divide between them. With 16 weeks of Government-Paid Maternity Leave and 4 weeks of Paternity Leave, that is up to 30 weeks of paid leave in the child's first year. It splits equally between the parents by default. Changing that split is a decision the parents make, and they have four weeks from the birth to submit it on LifeSG. The leave must be taken within 12 months of the birth, after the primary leave schemes are used up.
talkingPoint: An expecting client is budgeting for a year of reduced income. Thirty weeks of it is paid, and the default split is one they can change if they act within four weeks of the birth. Most find that out too late. Careful: It applies to Singapore Citizen children born on or after 1 April 2026; a birth before that falls under the 6-week scheme. Both parents must qualify for their own primary leave first.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

If your child is born on or after 1 April 2026 you get 10 weeks of Shared Parental Leave between you, on top of maternity and paternity leave: up to 30 weeks paid in the first year. The split defaults to half each, and you have four weeks after the birth to change it on LifeSG.

Source: Ministry of Social and Family Development, 1 Apr 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]
source: Ministry of Social and Family Development

title: Scams and Cybercrime Fell by Almost a Quarter in 2025
gist: Scam and cybercrime cases fell 24.8 per cent in 2025 to 41,974, and money lost fell from $1.1 billion to $913.1 million. The median loss per case still went up, from $1,389 to $1,644. Victims over 65 were only about 15 per cent of cases but lost the most each, an average of $37,053. In 81.8 per cent of cases the victim moved the money themselves. The scammer never touched the account.
talkingPoint: Read out the $37,053 line to anyone with an elderly parent. Then ask who would notice if that parent moved a large sum next week. Careful: This is a police statistic, not a product argument. Do not use it to imply any insurance or investment product prevents scam loss.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Scam cases fell in 2025, but the average elderly victim still lost $37,053, and in more than 8 in 10 cases the victim moved the money themselves.

Source: Singapore Police Force, 25 Feb 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Budget 2026 Highlights
gist: Singaporeans aged 50 and above in 2026, born in 1976 or earlier, get a CPF top-up of up to $1,500 in their Retirement Account or Special Account in December 2026. The amount is tiered by retirement savings and by the annual value of their home. The full $1,500 goes to those with less than $60,000 in retirement savings and a home with an annual value of $21,000 or less. Between $60,000 and 2026's Basic Retirement Sum of $110,200, it is $1,000. From January 2027, CPF contribution rates rise 1.5 percentage points for employees aged above 55 to 60, and 1.0 point for those above 60 to 65, fully allocated to the Retirement Account up to the Full Retirement Sum. A new CPF investment scheme with a small number of simplified, low-cost, life-cycle products arrives in the first half of 2028.
talkingPoint: Ask a client over 50 whether they know a top-up is landing in December, then ask what the balance it lands on is doing for the other eleven months. Careful: The top-up is tiered and not everyone gets $1,500. Check the client's retirement savings and their home's annual value against the table before naming a figure. These figures are from 12 Feb 2026. Check the source before you quote one.

title: AIA Singapore surpasses S$40 Billion in payouts over the last decade
gist: In the last decade AIA Singapore paid out more than S$40 billion in death, critical illness, accident, hospitalisation and maturity proceeds. The announcement marked the company's 95th anniversary in Singapore. AIA says it covers the health and wellness of over one third of the nation's workforce, and was the first insurer here to give policyholders mental health coverage.
talkingPoint: Every client privately wonders whether the company will actually pay. This is the answer with a number on it, and it is the insurer's own published figure, so they can check it. Careful: This is AIA's own release, not an independent audit, and a payout total is not a claims-approval rate. Never let it imply a particular claim will be paid; that turns on the policy wording.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Over the last ten years AIA Singapore paid out more than S$40 billion in claims and maturity proceeds. That is the part of a policy you never see until you need it.

Source: AIA Singapore, 12 Feb 2026. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: PM Wong's Budget 2026 in summary: AI, supporting workers, vouchers & helping businesses
gist: A S$154.69 billion Budget, delivered on 12 February 2026, built around an ambition to hold growth at the higher end of 2 to 3 per cent over the next decade. Eligible Singaporeans receive S$200 to S$400 in a Cost-of-Living Special Payment in September 2026, and up to S$570 in U-Save rebates over the financial year. Every Singaporean household gets S$500 in CDC vouchers in January 2027. Children aged 12 and below in 2026 receive S$500 in Child LifeSG credits.
talkingPoint: Put the payout dates on the table beside the client's own cashflow. Money that arrives on a known date is money that can be pointed at something. Careful: Eligibility differs for each payout. Never tell a client what they will receive without checking their own assessable income and property, which the Budget site sets out. These figures are from 12 Feb 2026. Check the source before you quote one.

title: More Singaporeans eligible for matching government grants for cash top-ups to boost retirement and healthcare savings
gist: The Government matches cash top-ups dollar for dollar: up to $2,000 a year under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme, capped at $20,000 over a lifetime. In 2026 around 750,000 Singaporeans are eligible for the expanded MRSS and around 185,000 for the new Matched MediSave Scheme. About 165,000 qualify for both, worth up to $3,000 of matching grants on top-ups made this year. MRSS paid out $456 million to more than 250,000 members for top-ups made in 2025, against $61 million to 103,000 members in 2024, after the age cap of 70 was removed and the grant raised to $2,000. From 1 January 2026 MRSS covers eligible Singaporeans with disabilities of all ages, not only those 55 and above. MMSS launched the same day as a five-year pilot. There is nothing to apply for. Eligibility is assessed automatically each year; the top-up is the only action.
talkingPoint: This is the one that makes a client sit up. The grant is free and automatic, but only on money they actually top up, so the people who need it most are the ones most likely to miss it. Check eligibility in front of them. Careful: Eligibility is income, property and balance tested and is assessed per year. Check the client's own position on the CPF site before naming a figure, and never imply the grant arrives without a top-up. These figures are from 26 Jan 2026. Check the source before you quote one.

title: New requirements for Integrated Shield Plan riders to strengthen sustainability of private health insurance and address rising healthcare costs
gist: From 1 April 2026, a new IP rider can no longer cover the minimum IP deductible, which runs from $1,500 to $3,500 a policy year depending on ward class. The co-payment cap rises to a minimum of $6,000 a policy year, from $3,000, and sits on top of that deductible. MOH said premiums for the new riders are expected to be about 30 per cent lower on average than existing riders with maximum coverage.
talkingPoint: This is the rule behind the letter your client received. Not their insurer's idea, not a downgrade aimed at them, and it landed on all seven insurers at once.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Every insurer had to change its rider on 1 April 2026. Your rider can no longer cover the first part of a bill, and the yearly cap on your share rose to $6,000.

Source: Ministry of Health, 26 Nov 2025. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Revision to Ministry of Health (MOH) Guidelines on Integrated Shield Plan Riders
gist: AIA published its own notice on 26 November 2025, the day MOH announced the rule change, and set out both changes plainly: no rider cover for the minimum deductible, and a co-payment cap moving from $3,000 to $6,000. Customers who bought an existing AIA Max VitalHealth rider between 27 November 2025 and 31 March 2026 keep it until it is updated, no later than their first renewal from 1 April 2028. That window covers all four withdrawn riders: Max VitalHealth A, A Value, B and B Lite.
talkingPoint: Ask when the client's insurer wrote to them about this. AIA's notice is dated the same day as the announcement and names the 2028 date in full. Careful: Other insurers published their own notices too. This is a card about clear, early communication, not a claim that anyone else hid anything.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

AIA's own note on the rider rule change, published the same day the Health Ministry announced it.

Source: AIA Singapore, 26 Nov 2025. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Double-digit medical cost increases projected to persist into 2026 and beyond in Singapore
gist: WTW's 2026 Global Medical Trends report puts Singapore at 16.9 per cent for 2026, after 15.5 per cent in 2025 and 12.3 per cent in 2024. That is above the Asia Pacific figure of 14 per cent and the global figure of 10.3 per cent. 77 per cent of insurers named new medical technologies as the top driver. Cancer is the single biggest condition behind the cost, named by 58 per cent of insurers in Asia Pacific. 57 per cent of insurers in the region expect the trend to keep rising over the next three years.
talkingPoint: Show the client the three-year line, then ask what they think the renewal letter will say in 2028. The plan they pick now is the one they will be paying for then. Careful: This is a survey of insurers' own expected claims cost trend, not official healthcare inflation. MOH publicly disputed reading it that way, so show the MOH reply on the same page. These figures are from 11 Nov 2025. Check the source before you quote one.

title: Adult bus & train fares in S'pore to go up by 9-10 cents from Dec. 27, 2025
gist: Adult card fares rose 9 to 10 cents a journey from 27 December 2025, an overall 5 per cent increase, below the 14.4 per cent the formula allowed. Concession fares rose 3 to 4 cents beyond 3.2km and were held flat below that. Cash fares rose more: 5 cents for students, 10 for seniors, 20 for adults. Monthly passes went the other way: $6 cheaper for adults and $3 for seniors. The Government put in $200 million of subsidy to hold the increase where it landed.
talkingPoint: Twenty cents a day is ninety dollars over a working year, for one person. It is the smallest number on this wall and the easiest one for a client to feel, which makes it a way into the cost-of-living conversation rather than the point of it. Careful: A fare change is cost of living, not a financial plan. Use it to open a budgeting conversation, never as an argument for a product. These figures are from 14 Oct 2025. Check the source before you quote one.

title: Government extends 4% interest rate floor on Special, MediSave and Retirement Account monies until 31 December 2026
gist: The 4 per cent floor on Special, MediSave and Retirement Account monies was extended for another year, from 1 January to 31 December 2026. The Ordinary Account pays 2.5 per cent, also a floor rate. Members under 55 earn an extra 1 per cent on the first $60,000 of combined balances. Members 55 and above earn an extra 2 per cent on the first $30,000 and an extra 1 per cent on the next $30,000. CPF named the reason in its own release: the falling interest rate environment.
talkingPoint: This is the answer to the savings-account objection, and it is not yours, it is the Government's. Put 4 per cent guaranteed beside what their bank is paying and let the client do the subtraction. Careful: The floor is extended a year at a time, not permanent, and CPF money is not available on demand the way a savings account is. Never compare the two on rate alone without saying that. These figures are from 22 Sep 2025. Check the source before you quote one.

title: Large Families to Receive $1,000 LifeSG Credits in September 2025
gist: For a third or subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025: the CDA First Step Grant rises by $5,000 to $10,000, plus a $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant paid into the mother's MediSave. On top of that, $1,000 a year in Large Family LifeSG Credits for each third and subsequent child, every year from the year the child turns one to the year they turn six. The first credits went out on 10 September 2025 to families with a third or subsequent child born between 2019 and 2024. After that they land every April. Announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong at Budget 2025.
talkingPoint: Ask a client with two children whether a third is on the table. If it is, this changes the arithmetic by $10,000 up front and $6,000 across the primary school years. Careful: Third or subsequent birth order only, and the grants are tied to a birth on or after 18 February 2025. The yearly credits run on their own eligibility date, so check LifeSG for the client's own position.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

If you have a third or subsequent child born from 18 February 2025, you get $10,000 into their CDA, $5,000 into your MediSave, and $1,000 a year in LifeSG credits from age one to six.

Source: Ministry of Social and Family Development, 10 Sep 2025. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]
source: Ministry of Social and Family Development

title: Government accepts CareShield Life Council's recommendations to enhance CareShield Life, provides additional $570 million to subsidise premiums
gist: CareShield Life payouts will grow at 4 per cent a year instead of 2 per cent, with the claims criteria unchanged. A policyholder claiming in 2030 gets $806 a month rather than $731. Premiums rise to pay for it, and the Government is putting over $570 million more into premium support over five years. All premiums stay fully payable from MediSave, and nobody loses cover for being unable to pay. Changes roll out progressively from January 2026. Alongside it: the Home Caregiving Grant rises to up to $600 a month from April 2026, and long-term care service subsidies go up to a maximum of 80 per cent from July 2026.
talkingPoint: Severe disability is the risk clients insure last and fear most. Put $806 a month beside what a nursing home actually costs and let the gap do the talking. Careful: CareShield Life covers severe disability only, on its own claims criteria. Never present the payout as a general income replacement, and never imply it meets the full cost of care.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

CareShield Life payouts will grow twice as fast from 2026, reaching $806 a month for someone claiming in 2030. It is designed to cover basic long-term care needs, not the whole cost.

Source: Ministry of Health, 27 Aug 2025. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Extension of the holding period of Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) and higher SSD rates for residential properties
gist: For residential property bought on or after 4 July 2025, the SSD holding period went from three years back to four, and every tier rose by four percentage points. The new rates: 16 per cent if sold within a year, 12 per cent within two, 8 per cent within three, and 4 per cent within four. Nothing after four years. MAS gave the reason plainly: short-holding-period transactions had risen sharply, especially sub-sales of units that have not been completed. HDB owners are unaffected, because the Minimum Occupation Period already covers them.
talkingPoint: Anyone who bought private property after July 2025 has a four-year clock running. Ask when they bought before any conversation about selling to release money. Careful: It applies only to property acquired on or after 4 July 2025. A client who bought before that keeps the old three-year schedule, so check the purchase date before quoting a rate.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

If you bought a private property on or after 4 July 2025 and sell within four years, you pay Seller's Stamp Duty: 16 per cent in year one, tapering to 4 per cent in year four. It does not apply to HDB flats.

Source: Monetary Authority of Singapore, 3 Jul 2025. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Prudential, AIA still offering pre-authorisation at Mount Elizabeth hospitals despite Great Eastern's shock move
gist: Prudential and AIA told The Business Times they were still issuing pre-authorisation certificates for any healthcare institution. AIA's own pre-authorisation page continues to offer the service for admissions, day surgery and outpatient cancer treatment, with assessment in 3 working days of a complete doctor submission.
talkingPoint: Same week, same hospitals, two different answers. That is what a wider hospital position is worth on the day it matters. Careful: Prudential is named alongside AIA in this headline, so use it as an AIA strength, not as a Prudential attack. Pre-authorisation practice can change at any insurer, so never promise it is permanent.

title: MOH engaging insurer to better understand suspension of Mount Elizabeth pre-authorisation
gist: Within two days the suspension went from a commercial decision to something the Ministry of Health was publicly engaging the insurer about. MOH said it was seeking to understand the basis for the suspension and its impact on policyholders.
talkingPoint: A pre-authorisation policy that pulls in the Health Ministry is not a small print detail. It is the difference between walking in and paying up front.

title: Insurer Great Eastern pauses pre-authorisation certificates for Mount Elizabeth admissions
gist: From 17 June 2025, Great Eastern stopped issuing pre-authorisation certificates for Mount Elizabeth Hospital and Mount Elizabeth Novena. Great Eastern said cover and claims were unchanged. Without pre-authorisation, a patient can still be asked to settle the bill first and claim after. IHH Healthcare said it was in active discussion with the insurer and was surprised by a unilateral move made before those talks concluded.
talkingPoint: Ask the client which hospital they would want if the diagnosis were serious, then ask whether their insurer will still pre-authorise it.

title: A guide to the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant and Proximity Grant
gist: First-timer couples and families can get up to $120,000 in Enhanced CPF Housing Grant, on a new BTO or a resale flat, tapering with household income. The income ceiling is $9,000 average gross monthly household income. Applying as a first-timer alongside a second-timer halves it. The buyer or their spouse must have worked continuously for the 12 months before applying, and still be employed at application. The grant goes into the CPF Ordinary Account, not into their hands as cash. The Proximity Housing Grant is separate, for a resale flat bought to live with or near parents or married children.
talkingPoint: A young client saving a cash deposit often has no idea the grant lands in CPF rather than in the bank. That changes what they need in cash, and it changes what they can afford to keep invested. Careful: The amount tapers steeply with income and the 12-month employment rule catches people who have just switched jobs. Check the client's own figure on CPF or HDB before quoting one.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Buying your first flat, you may get up to $120,000 in Enhanced CPF Housing Grant if your household earns $9,000 a month or less. It is paid into your CPF Ordinary Account, not as cash, and you need 12 months of continuous work behind you.

Source: CPF Board, 9 May 2025. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Closure of Special Account for CPF members aged 55 and above and other CPF enhancements
gist: The Special Accounts of about 1.4 million members aged 55 and above were closed on 19 January 2025. Savings moved to the Retirement Account up to the member's cohort Full Retirement Sum, where they keep the long-term rate. Anything left went to the Ordinary Account at 2.5 per cent. A member can move that Ordinary Account money into the Retirement Account, up to the year's Enhanced Retirement Sum, to earn 4 per cent and a higher payout. CPF states plainly that the transfer is irreversible. The Enhanced Retirement Sum rose on 1 January 2025 from three times to four times the Basic Retirement Sum: $426,000 in 2025, and someone turning 55 that year who tops up to it can draw CPF LIFE payouts of up to $3,300 a month for life from 65.
talkingPoint: The question every client over 55 has is whether to move the Ordinary Account money across. 2.5 against 4 per cent is the easy half. The word that decides it is irreversible, so say that one out loud. Careful: The Enhanced Retirement Sum changes every year, so 2025's $426,000 and the $3,300 payout belong to that cohort. Quote the current year's figure for a client deciding today, and never present the transfer as reversible. These figures are from 19 Jan 2025. Check the source before you quote one.

title: MAS and IMDA announce implementation of Shared Responsibility Framework from 16 December 2024
gist: From 16 December 2024, banks, payment providers and telcos carry defined duties against phishing scams, and are expected to pay out where a duty was breached. The duties include a 12-hour cooling-off period after a digital token is activated or a login happens on a new device, a 24/7 reporting channel, and a self-service kill switch to block account access. After consultation MAS added a duty of real-time fraud surveillance aimed at account-draining transactions, in recognition of how severe those cases are. It covers phishing where a scammer impersonates a legitimate business or government body and the victim enters credentials on a fake site or app.
talkingPoint: Clients assume a scam loss is always theirs to carry. It depends on whether the bank met its duties, and most have never heard of the kill switch they already have. Careful: The framework covers phishing only. It does not cover a scam where the victim knowingly authorises a payment, such as an investment or love scam, and a payout is not automatic. Never tell a client they will be reimbursed.
clientMessage:
Hi [Client name],

Since December 2024, banks and telcos have defined anti-scam duties and are expected to pay out if they miss one. It covers phishing, where you are tricked into entering your credentials on a fake site, and your bank already gives you a kill switch to freeze your account.

Source: Monetary Authority of Singapore, 24 Oct 2024. If you'd like, we can look at what this means for your own plan.

[Your name]

title: Singapore blocks Allianz deal for Income Insurance but open to new offer, PM says
gist: The Government blocked Allianz's proposed majority stake, worth around S$2.2 billion, on public interest grounds on 14 October 2024, and the Insurance Act was amended. Allianz withdrew its pre-conditional offer on 16 December 2024. The episode resurfaced as a campaign issue at the 2025 general election.
talkingPoint: Only raise this if the client brings up Income, and keep it to ownership and direction. Careful: Nothing in this story is about claims handling or policyholder service. Do not present it as one.

title: Government accepts MediShield Life Council's recommendations to enhance MediShield Life scheme, Government support more than offsets premium increases
gist: MediShield Life premiums rise by up to 35 per cent in total, phased evenly over three years from April 2025 to March 2028, an average of about 22 per cent per policyholder by the third year. Cover rose with the price: the policy year limit from $150,000 to $200,000, the normal ward daily limit from $1,000 to $1,630, and the ICU daily limit from $2,200 to $5,140. The inpatient deductible rises by up to $1,500, and a $500 outpatient deductible starts on 1 June 2026. The Government put $4.1 billion of support, in MediSave top-ups and subsidies, against $1.8 billion of premium increases.
talkingPoint: Every Shield plan sits on MediShield Life, so part of the increase is not the insurer's at all. Separate the two before the client blames the wrong one. Careful: Check which phase the client is in before quoting a figure. The second phase of the inpatient deductible increase only starts on 1 April 2027. These figures are from 15 Oct 2024. Check the source before you quote one.

title: Aviva to exit Singlife joint venture
gist: Aviva agreed to sell its 25.9 per cent stake in Singlife, plus two debt instruments, for a total of 0.8 billion pounds. Aviva Singapore had merged with Singlife only three years earlier, in 2020. Sumitomo Life went on to take full ownership of Singlife in 2024, in a deal valuing it at S$4.6 billion.
talkingPoint: Aviva Singapore customers have been through two owners since 2020. Ask what that continuity is worth on a policy meant to last a lifetime. Careful: Ownership only. Do not imply a change of owner weakens a policyholder's contractual cover.

title: HSBC completes acquisition of AXA Singapore
gist: HSBC completed the purchase of 100 per cent of AXA Insurance Pte Ltd on 11 February 2022, after announcing it on 16 August 2021. AXA Singapore was folded into HSBC Life, so AXA Shield policyholders became HSBC Life policyholders. With the Allianz sale agreed in July 2026 and due to close in 2027, the same book of policies is lined up for its third owner in five years, pending MAS approval.
talkingPoint: Read the two headlines side by side. AXA in 2022, Allianz agreed in 2026. Ask your client who they think they will be insured with in ten years. Careful: HSBC said at the time there was no change to the terms of policies in force. Say that too, then make the point about continuity rather than cover.
